newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish yields to rise Monday, market eyes budget.
newsitem.headline: Polish yields to rise Monday, market eyes budget.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to inch up at Monday's 1.2 billion zloty primary auction as uncertainty over next year's budget and inflation is persuading banks to search for better terms at tenders, analysts said.

They said the government's inflation target of year-on-year 13 percent in December 1997 was not realistic if the budget exceeds 2.6 percent of gross domestic product, and the latest government proposal sets next year's budget gap at 2.8 percent.
"If the government wants a bigger budget deficit...it will have to pay for it with higher yields," said a senior dealer at a foreign bank in Warsaw.
Analysts expected the minimum price for the benchmark 52-week T-bill, last at 83.53, to inch down toward 83.50 as investors take advantage of the treasury's large offer.
"The finance ministry may have to let the benchmark go a grosz or two at next Monday's auction," said Wojciech Kowalczyk, senior treasury dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.

Analysts said the bids for the shorter bills offered on Monday, maturing in 26- and 13-weeks, would come from domestic non-financial investors because they were not attractive for Polish banks, which could bid for higher yielding NBP-bills.
They said the minimum price for the 26-week bill should hold steady or inch down a fraction to around 91.15 and to 95.50 for the 13-week paper.
Analysts said the duration of the present upward correction in T-bill yields, which fell rapidly in the third quarter of 1996, would depend on what budget is passed for next year.
"It depends on the budget and taxes, because they will tell banks what inflation to expect next year," said Rafal Chodzidlo, senior dealer at Bank Slaski SA.

One-day deposit rates are expected to stabilise around 20 percent next week after this week's rush to square required reserves before the end of the October period pushed call-money rates up to the 25 percent lombard rate, analysts said.
"Banks' liquidity may get a boost early next week from surpluses coming from clearing house receipts," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz, chief dealer at PKO BP.
"However rates should not fall from Friday's levels next week. One should get used to rates around 20 percent as far as one-day deposits are concerned," Wieczorkiewicz added.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates closed the week straddling the 20 percent level at 19.90/20.30 and 19.60/20.10.

The zloty was seen remaining in its weeks-old trading band between 1.6 and 1.9 percent from the central parity and tracking world dollar/mark moves as no large domestic forces were seen affecting the Polish currency.
The Polish currency closed at 2.8120/35 per dollar and at 1.8580/90 per mark, or about 1.85 percent from the parity rate.
